strategy_title: Autotune num_warps/num_stages Without Reducing Tile Sizes Causes Regression
strategy_description: When the plan called for autotuning tile sizes (BLOCK_M, BLOCK_N, BLOCK_K) to reduce register pressure, the actual diff only changed the fixed tile values (BLOCK_M=128, BLOCK_N=32, BLOCK_K=64) and added autotune configs that only swept num_warps and num_stages — leaving tile sizes as hardcoded constexprs. The larger BLOCK_M=128 and BLOCK_K=64 increased registers/thread from 96 to 128 and dynamic shared memory from 32 KB to 122 KB per block, collapsing Block Limit Shared Mem from 5 to 1 block/SM. This drove theoretical occupancy from 31.25% down to 6.25%, active warps/scheduler from 4.76 to 1.0, and compute throughput from 76.6% to 41.56%, nearly doubling kernel duration. The anti-pattern is: increasing tile sizes while adding autotune for only num_warps/num_stages will worsen occupancy if shared memory becomes the binding constraint.
slow_pseudocode:
# Before: fixed small tiles, moderate register/smem usage
BLOCK_M = 64; BLOCK_N = 64; BLOCK_K = 32  # constexpr
# 96 regs/thread, 32 KB smem/block -> 5 blocks/SM, 31% occupancy
@triton.jit
def kernel(A, B, C): ...
fast_pseudocode:
# Intended: autotune over tile sizes to find register-efficient config
# Actual diff: only swept num_warps/num_stages, hardcoded larger tiles
BLOCK_M = 128; BLOCK_N = 32; BLOCK_K = 64  # constexpr (larger!)
@triton.autotune(configs=[Config({}, num_warps=4, num_stages=4), ...], key=[])
@triton.jit
def kernel(A, B, C): ...
# 128 regs/thread, 122 KB smem/block -> 1 block/SM, 6% occupancy
applicable_when: Kernel is register- or shared-memory-bound with low theoretical occupancy; plan intends to reduce tile sizes via autotune to lower register pressure.
do_not_apply_when: Tile sizes are not actually swept in autotune configs (i.e., BLOCK_M/BLOCK_N/BLOCK_K remain hardcoded constexprs); increasing any tile dimension will worsen shared memory pressure and collapse occupancy further.
framework_notes: In Triton, if BLOCK_M/BLOCK_N/BLOCK_K are tl.constexpr inside the kernel body rather than kernel arguments, @triton.autotune configs cannot change them — they must be promoted to kernel arguments for autotune to sweep them. Configs with empty dicts ({}) only control num_warps and num_stages, not tile sizes.
